codes.title: Gout
codes.rationale: The clinical presentation of sudden severe pain, swelling, erythema, and exquisite tenderness of the first metatarsophalangeal joint in a patient with diabetes is classic for gout. GDL-013 explicitly states that classic history and typical joint distribution carry weight in patients with diabetes, and the absence of alternative explanations (e.g., trauma, infection) supports this assignment. Fever is noted but does not exclude gout, and the guideline does not require synovial fluid analysis for assignment in this context.

evidence.quote: Woke two days ago with severe pain and swelling at the base of the right big toe. Joint now red, shiny and so tender he cannot bear the weight of the bedsheet on it.
Gout; gouty arthritis; podagra

Sudden severe pain, swelling and erythema of the first metatarsophalangeal joint waking the patient from sleep, with exquisite tenderness to light touch, is the classic gout presentation, and the gout entry applies where that joint is the sole site of concern and systemic features are absent.

codes.title: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
codes.rationale: The patient has documented type 2 diabetes on metformin, which is explicitly stated in the note. GDL-011 directs assignment to the corresponding type entry when the type is stated.

evidence.quote: 52M, type 2 diabetes on metformin, HbA1c 7.8 last month.
Type 2 diabetes mellitus; T2DM; non-insulin-dependent diabetes
Where the record states the diabetes type, assign the corresponding type entry.

codes.title: Fever of unknown origin
codes.rationale: Fever (38.3°C) is documented but not accounted for by the gout assignment alone. GDL-001 states that symptom codes apply only when no established condition accounts for the symptom. Here, gout does not fully explain the fever, and no other condition is established. Thus, fever is coded separately.

evidence.quote: Temp 38.3 today and reports feeling shivery overnight.
Fever of unknown origin; pyrexia of unknown origin; PUO

Chapter 21 assignments record a presenting symptom where the encounter closes without an established underlying diagnosis. Where the record documents a condition that accounts for the symptom, the condition carries the assignment and the symptom is not separately coded.

candidates.title: Septic arthritis
candidates.missing_discriminator: synovial fluid microscopy and culture results (to confirm bacterial infection) or clinical evidence of systemic toxicity (e.g., hypotension, severe sepsis) or rapid progression of symptoms. GDL-021 and GDL-032 note that fever and acute joint pain in diabetes may require aspiration to rule out septic arthritis, but the classic gout presentation and absence of systemic toxicity or ascending infection make this less likely.

candidates.title: Cutaneous abscess
candidates.missing_discriminator: evidence of a localized collection of pus (e.g., fluctuance, pointing) or ascending cellulitis. The note explicitly states no ulcer or ascending redness, and the pain is localized to the joint, not the skin.

confidence_rationale: The clinical presentation (sudden severe pain, swelling, erythema, and exquisite tenderness of the first MTP joint) is classic for gout, and GDL-013 explicitly supports this assignment in patients with diabetes. The type 2 diabetes assignment is high confidence due to explicit documentation. Fever is coded as a symptom because it is not accounted for by gout alone, and no alternative diagnosis is established.
would_raise_confidence: Synovial fluid microscopy showing monosodium urate crystals or a documented serum urate level would confirm gout. Negative synovial fluid culture would exclude septic arthritis.
would_lower_confidence: Documentation of systemic toxicity (e.g., hypotension, altered mental status) or ascending infection (e.g., cellulitis) would raise suspicion for septic arthritis and lower confidence in the gout assignment.

codes.title: Giant cell arteritis
codes.rationale: The patient presents with new-onset unilateral headache, jaw claudication, temporal tenderness, and markedly elevated inflammatory markers (ESR 88, CRP 62), which are classic features of giant cell arteritis. The age (62F) and absence of prior headaches further support this diagnosis. The guideline GDL-014 explicitly states that new headache after age 50 with jaw discomfort on chewing, scalp tenderness, and raised inflammatory markers should be evaluated along the large-vessel vasculitis pathway, with giant cell arteritis as the primary consideration.

codes.title: Severe pre-eclampsia
codes.rationale: New hypertension (BP ≥160 systolic) after 20 weeks of gestation with proteinuria (3+ on dipstick) and symptoms (headache, visual disturbance) meets the criteria for severe pre-eclampsia. The guideline GDL-028 explicitly states that systolic pressure ≥160 is a severity feature moving the assignment to the severe entry.

evidence.quote: 29F, G2P1, 30+2 weeks by dating scan. Two days of headache across the forehead and flashing lights in her vision this morning. Swelling of hands and face noticed by her husband. BP 168/112, repeated after 15 minutes 165/110. Urine dipstick protein 3+
Severe pre-eclampsia

New hypertension arising after twenty weeks of gestation with proteinuria, or with any of headache, visual disturbance, right upper quadrant or epigastric pain, hyperreflexia or a falling platelet count, is pre-eclampsia. Severity features moving the assignment to the severe entry are systolic pressure at or above 160, platelets below 100, deranged transaminases, or pulmonary oedema.

confidence_rationale: The documented findings (new hypertension after 20 weeks, proteinuria, headache, visual disturbance, and brisk reflexes) satisfy the criteria for severe pre-eclampsia as per GDL-028. No competing entry accounts for the same findings equally well.
would_raise_confidence: Documentation of platelets, transaminases, or pulmonary oedema would further confirm severity but is not required for the current assignment.
would_lower_confidence: Absence of proteinuria or a lower systolic BP would reduce confidence in the severe pre-eclampsia diagnosis.
